glm.feedback:
## Findings

- Category: spec / edge-case
  Severity: medium
  File: shared/scripts/tools/verifiers/review_record_closure.py:100–116 (with iteration-reviews.md:645–650)
  Finding: The docs state "rows in already-merged records are legacy and are never re-verified," but `reason_codes_closed` has no cutoff — it fails any `not_run`/`not_applicable` row without a `reason_code`, including rows written before this change. Since `_no_entry_detail` (in `_entry_details.py`) explicitly contemplates re-verifying *older* runs from the tree, re-running F11 on any pre-U3 run whose rows are within the retention window will now fail on legacy codeless rows — contradicting the documented contract.
  Suggestion: Either gate `reason_codes_closed` on a cutoff (e.g. skip rows whose run predates this change, or consult the `commit_hash` param already threaded into `check_review_record`), or soften the doc claim to "the current F11 run is not re-run on merged records."

- Category: spec
  Severity: low
  File: shared/scripts/tools/verifiers/review_record_closure.py:63–99 (with iteration-reviews.md:654–659)
  Finding: The docs say from `small` up "each type names its OWN code" (e.g. `plan_internal` → `complexity-below-threshold`), but the enforcement only checks (a) a code is present and (b) it isn't `trivial-auto`. A uniform `close-missing --reason-code diff-below-threshold` applied to all seven types — including `plan` and `external_code`, for which the docs prescribe other codes — passes the gate. The tests themselves rely on this (`test_record_review_pass_cli_floor._close_missing` defaults every type to `diff-below-threshold` at small and asserts `.ok`), so the enforced contract is weaker than the documented one.
  Suggestion: Either add a per-type code map to `reason_codes_closed` (at least for the types with an unambiguous code), or state in the docs that any non-`trivial-auto` code is accepted from small up.

- Category: test
  Severity: low
  File: shared/tests/test_review_record_closure.py:100–107
  Finding: `test_an_evidence_free_self_row_fails` uses `make_entry("self", "completed", recorded_by="none")`. Whether this actually fails depends on `carries_evidence` treating the literal string `"none"` as non-evidence — a magic value not documented in the diff. If `carries_evidence` only checks non-blankness, this test would fail for the wrong reason (or the implementation needs a special case). Worth pinning the intended semantics.
  Suggestion: Either record the self row with `recorded_by=None` (the actual "nobody earned it" shape the module docstring describes) or document that `"none"` is a recognized null adapter in `carries_evidence`.

- Category: edge-case
  Severity: low
  File: shared/scripts/tools/verifiers/review_record_closure.py:33–56
  Finding: When the `self` row is absent entirely, `entry_for(record, "self")` presumably yields an empty/pending row; if the earlier pending check does not materialize `self` as pending (it was described as materialized "up front" for live runs, but hand-built fixtures may omit it), `self_review_recorded` reports `` `self` is '' `` — a confusing empty-status message. Minor, but the message should distinguish "absent" from a status.
  Suggestion: Branch on an absent row and say "`self` has no row" before formatting the status.

Everything else checks out: the extraction from `iterate_checks.py` preserves the public import surface (and a test pins it), the ledger trivial-row logic correctly refuses `trivial-auto` above trivial and accepts justification-or-enumeration at trivial, `close-missing`-cannot-complete-self is exercised, campaign roundtrip tests were updated with the new codes, and new tests are tagged `pytest.mark.covers` per the campaign contract. No security issues introduced — all inputs are file-backed JSON validated against closed vocabularies.

Overall: ship-with-fixes — the core U3 behavior is correctly implemented and well-tested; the doc-vs-enforcement gaps above (especially the legacy-record promise) should be reconciled before merge.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
